notes.n7.api: Regional token APIs (EU: Scaleway, IONOS, STACKIT, OVHcloud, Lyceum; India: Sarvam, Pipeshift, E2E; Japan: Sakura) compete on data residency rather than price.
notes.n7.platform: Each hyperscaler runs a multi-model platform (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex, OCI, watsonx); in China, ByteDance Volcano Engine, Alibaba Bailian, Baidu Qianfan and Tencent compete hard on token price.
notes.n7.engine: Consolidating on two open-source engines, vLLM and SGLang, each spun into a VC-backed company in Jan 2026 (Inferact $150M seed; RadixArk ~$100M seed); NVIDIA pushes TensorRT-LLM and Dynamo; HF TGI is in maintenance mode.
notes.n7.local: Built on llama.cpp/ggml (team joined Hugging Face Feb 2026) and Apple MLX; platform owners (Apple, Google, Qualcomm, Microsoft, Meta) control the NPU runtimes; 1-bit/compressed models (PrismML) are pushing larger models on-device.
notes.n7.opt: 2026 brought large rounds for optimisation pure-plays (Gimlet $80M A, Wafer $40M A, Inferact $150M seed).
notes.n7.compress: Thin, early segment: providers' own prompt/context caching (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Bedrock) is the default; independent prompt/context-compression startups are seed-stage (The Token Company, Compresr - YC) plus Tileward, which pairs context compaction with compressed models; LLMLingua is the open-source reference.
notes.n7.route: Biggest 2026 consolidation: Palo Alto Networks closed Portkey (May 2026) and Stripe agreed to buy OpenRouter (Aug 2026, reported >$7B after a $1.3B Series B in May); gateways are being pulled into security (PANW, F5), API management (Kong, Solo.io) and payments (Stripe); open-source LiteLLM remains the default self-hosted proxy.
notes.n7.obs: LLM observability is being absorbed by data/infra platforms: Langfuse to ClickHouse (Jan 2026), Helicone to Mintlify (Mar 2026), OpenMeter to Kong (Sep 2025), W&B to CoreWeave (2025); cost attribution (CloudZero, Vantage, Pay-i, Revenium) overlaps with n4.finops.
notes.n7.private: Hyperscalers and Apple/Google now offer enclave-based private AI; startups (Opaque, Edgeless, Tinfoil) sell attested confidential inference; on-prem demand served by Cohere, Mistral and server OEMs.
notes.n7.bench: Fragmented: independent analysts (Artificial Analysis, SemiAnalysis), non-profits (MLCommons, Epoch), crowd arenas (LMArena) and Chinese leaderboards (OpenCompass, SuperCLUE).
